name: Save and resume web drafts (autosave + guest clear on success)

arm-01.note: 500ms-debounced autosave to a server draft plus a localStorage mirror; a dedicated success route explicitly clears the guest cookie/token hash on successful checkout only, and this exact behavior is covered by p4-smoke.ts.

arm-02.note: 800ms-debounced autosave with stale-response guarding (pendingEditsRef); guest drafts keyed by HMAC-hashed random token in an httpOnly cookie; completeDraft() clears the guest cookie ONLY on successful checkout, never on abandonment — exactly matches the spec.

arm-03.note: No separate 'autosave' step — each cart mutation is a direct server-action write, so there's nothing to debounce or lose; a guestClearedAt field exists to support clearing on success.

arm-04.note: Same direct-persistence-per-action model as arm-03; clearGuestToken() is called when a guest's draft is claimed at sign-in during checkout, not exactly gated on 'checkout success' but functionally close.

arm-05.note: 700ms-debounced autosave to a server draft keyed by an access token stored in sessionStorage (not httpOnly cookie — more exposed to XSS than the other arms' approach); resumes on reload via sessionStorage id. Guest-clear-on-success behavior not directly verified in the reviewed slice.

arm-06.note: Explicit design comment: signed-in customers autosave to a server draft; guests autosave to localStorage and only get a server draft + httpOnly-cookie access token at checkout identity capture; guest copy clears ONLY on success/explicit cancel, never on refresh — matches the spec intent, though guest state living in localStorage before checkout is a smaller attack surface than a cookie-backed draft from the first keystroke.

arm-01.note: 32-byte random token, SHA-256 hashed at rest, httpOnly/sameSite=lax cookie; findAccessibleDraft() never accepts a client-supplied draft id without a matching token/session.

arm-02.note: Random 32-byte token minted for guests, httpOnly/sameSite=lax cookie, only the HMAC of the token stored in DB (raw token never persisted) — anti-enumeration by design since no API accepts a draft id from the client.

arm-03.note: 24-byte token hashed with a secret+version salt, per-draft tokenVersion supports rotation, timing-safe compare, uniform 404s so a wrong-principal request can't tell a draft exists — the most rigorous guest-token design of the six.

arm-04.note: 32-byte token, SHA-256 hashed, httpOnly cookie via shared BROWSER_COOKIE_OPTIONS, clean DraftOwner union type keeps guest/customer/POS ownership from ever being conflated.

arm-05.note: Guest token exists and is sent via a custom x-draft-access-token header, but the raw token is kept in sessionStorage on the client rather than an httpOnly cookie — more exposed to XSS/theft than the clone cluster or arm-06's cookie-based approach.

arm-06.note: generateGuestToken/hashGuestToken/verifyGuestToken with url-safe random tokens, hashed storage, httpOnly cookie delivery, and dedicated unit checks (scripts/test-p4.mts) covering uniqueness, determinism, and rejection of wrong/null tokens.

arm-02.note: finalizeOrder() flips status in a guarded transaction, reserves aggregated tracked inventory (throwing/rolling back the whole finalize on shortfall), claims a per-season sequential number via a single atomic UPDATE...RETURNING, folds lines into packages with an advisory-lock-protected find-or-create, and enqueues lifecycle emails in the same transaction.

arm-03.note: lib/orders/finalize.ts's finalizeOrder() locks the season row (FOR UPDATE) to claim the next order number, reserves inventory, groups lines into packages, and is the single implementation called from the Stripe webhook, the offline-payment poster, and the ops console — no duplicate path.

arm-02.note: This codebase has zero Next.js Server Actions ('use server') anywhere -- all mutations go through API routes, so the item's literal subject doesn't exist in this architecture. name: Auditable staged import pipeline + atomic commits
